title: QUIC internal congestion-controller selector architecture
purpose: Describe how the transport core can keep an internal construction-time congestion-controller selector per path, default to NewReno, permit CUBIC only under the existing RFC 9002 and RFC 8085 invariants, and preserve deterministic path-local recovery state and monotonic timing.
design_summary: Each path owns its own congestion-controller selection and controller state. The selector runs at path construction time, stores a private controller kind in the path state, and never exposes that choice as a public API or a caller-selectable transport option. Default paths instantiate the NewReno controller and must remain observationally equivalent to the existing RFC 9002 NewReno homes. An internal CUBIC implementation is allowed only as a private path-local choice that still satisfies the RFC 9002 recovery and congestion invariants plus the RFC 8085 congestion-control guidelines. The controller state uses the existing monotonic clock seam so every elapsed-time decision stays deterministic and replayable in tests. Path promotion and migration may reset or restore controller state only through the existing path-state semantics, and ACK, loss, ECN, persistent congestion, and PMTU-normalized window math all stay inside the same per-path controller boundary.
alternatives_considered: Expose a public controller-selection API. Rejected because the selector is an internal construction-time policy and must not become part of the supported surface.
Hot-swap the controller after path creation. Rejected because the choice must remain immutable for the life of the path and the state machine becomes harder to reason about.
Use a single connection-wide controller shared across all paths. Rejected because RFC 9002 congestion control is per path and migration resets/restores are path-local.
Make CUBIC the default controller. Rejected because the existing NewReno requirement homes are the canonical baseline and must remain the default proof home.
edge_cases_and_constraints: Path construction is the only time the selector may choose NewReno versus CUBIC.
Path promotion and migration may reset or restore controller state, but they may not create a new public controller choice.
Monotonic clock reads must not depend on wall-clock time or on local system adjustments.
ACK-only packets, loss signals, ECN signals, and persistent congestion remain path-local recovery inputs.
PMTU or MSS normalization must feed the same controller math for both controller choices.
data_and_state_considerations: The controller choice can live as a small immutable field on each path record, while the mutable congestion-control and recovery state stays with the same path record or a nested controller state object. The selector must not reach endpoint-shared state, and it must not cache a public-facing notion of supported controllers. Time comparisons should use the monotonic-clock abstraction so tests can replay controller transitions deterministically. When a path is discarded, its controller state is discarded with it; when a path is revalidated or promoted, only the existing path-state semantics may decide whether state is reset or restored.
risks: If the selector leaks into public API or support text, the internal-only boundary is lost.
If the default NewReno path diverges from the current RFC 9002 homes, the selector will look correct while silently changing the shipped baseline.
If the monotonic time seam is replaced with wall-clock time, controller behavior will become nondeterministic under test and load.
If CUBIC is allowed to bypass the RFC 9002 and RFC 8085 invariants, the selector will widen support beyond the intended proof boundary.
